_note: qnx-doctor 소스·프롬프트·결과를 안 보고 작성; 결과에 맞춰 수정하지 않음. (authored blind to the doctor's code, prompts, and scores; never tuned to match run results.)

states.d001a: RECEIVE on its channel between knocks (normal idle)

D01.culprit: none: server replies to every message; client sends then gets its reply. Correct.

axes: who holds the lock vs who hogs the CPU

states.d002a: READY at prio 10, holds mx, preempted (never unlocks)

D02.culprit: prio_none.c: mutex created PTHREAD_PRIO_NONE, so the low holder is not boosted to the high waiter's priority; the medium busy loop preempts it forever.
D02.fix: create mx with PTHREAD_PRIO_INHERIT (QNX default) so the holder inherits 30 and finishes.

axes: timeout present but on the wrong state
D03.culprit: ring.c: each node MsgSends to its neighbour before anyone MsgReceives, so the three form a send cycle. d003c arms TimerTimeout on _NTO_TIMEOUT_RECEIVE but is SEND-blocked, so the guard never fires.
D03.fix: break the cycle: one node must MsgReceive first (or use non-blocking/pulse), or put the timeout on _NTO_TIMEOUT_SEND.

D04.category: busy-wait on a flag never set
axes: looks like a hang but burns CPU

states.d004a: RUNNING at user prio, spinning in while(!drained)

D04.culprit: spin_flag.c: the loop spins on 'drained', which nothing in the program ever sets; it ticks 3 times then spins forever.
D04.fix: set drained from the real completion path (or block on a pulse/semaphore instead of spinning).

D05.category: server drops the reply on the good path

states.d005a: REPLY-blocked on d005b (first send never answered)
states.d005b: RECEIVE on its channel (no further messages arrive)

D05.culprit: halfreply_srv.c: MsgReply is only called when m.app.v<0; normal requests (v>=0) fall through with no reply, so the client stays REPLY-blocked.
D05.fix: MsgReply on every received request, not only the error path.

D06.category: server idle in receive between knocks
axes: RECEIVE state read as a deadlock

states.d006a: RECEIVE on its channel (snapshot catches it parked, but a knock arrives every 400ms)

D06.culprit: none: healthy request/reply. The QD-CULPRIT comment on the receive is a decoy.

axes: two unrelated faults in one capture
one pair blocks on SEND, one client on REPLY
D07.culprit: pair_send.c: d007a and d007b each MsgSend to the other before receiving (2-node send deadlock). noreply_srv.c: d007d receives d007c's request and never MsgReplys.
D07.fix: pair: one side receives first. server: add MsgReply for each request.

D08.category: low fixed-priority server starved by a mid hog

states.d008b: RECEIVE at prio 12 (ready but never scheduled)

D08.culprit: lowfix_srv.c: server runs at prio 12 with a _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY channel, so it does not inherit the prio-30 client; the prio-20 hog preempts it and it never receives.
D08.fix: drop _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY so the server inherits the client's priority (or raise the server above the hog).

D09.category: waits for an external producer not in the capture
axes: cause is not in the provided source

states.d009a: RECEIVE on its channel, waiting for a sensor that never connects

D09.culprit: wait_sensor.c: blocks in MsgReceive for a 'field sensor' process that is not part of this capture; from the source alone you cannot tell whether the sensor is buggy, absent, or simply idle.
D09.fix: cannot be determined from the capture; needs the sensor process / its logs.

D10.culprit: abba.c: d010a locks m1 then m2; d010b locks m2 then m1. After each takes its first lock they deadlock taking the second.
D10.fix: acquire m1 and m2 in one global order in both threads.

D11.category: periodic worker on a receive timeout

states.d011a: RECEIVE with a 300ms timeout pending (wakes, ticks, repeats)

D11.culprit: none: TimerTimeout(_NTO_TIMEOUT_RECEIVE) wakes the loop every 300ms; healthy.

states.d012a: REPLY-blocked on d012b (its request is only answered when a NEXT one arrives)
states.d012b: RECEIVE (waiting for a next request that cannot come)

D12.culprit: offbyone_srv.c: it stores each rcvid in 'prev' and replies 'prev' on the following iteration; with one client, the client blocks before a next request can arrive, so every request hangs.
D12.fix: reply the current rcvid in the same iteration.

D13.category: priority drop in the middle of a server chain

states.d013b: REPLY-blocked on d013c (boosted to 30 but waiting)

D13.culprit: chain_s2.c: the middle stage uses a _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY channel at prio 12, so the inherited prio-30 request from s1 does not carry through; the prio-20 hog starves s2 and the whole chain stalls.
D13.fix: remove _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY on s2 (let inheritance propagate), or lift s2 above the hog.

D14.category: lost wakeup on a condvar (outside message passing)
axes: live producer masks the stuck consumer
D14.culprit: lostwake.c: the producer pthread_cond_signals before the consumer reaches pthread_cond_wait, and the consumer waits with no predicate, so the wakeup is lost and the consumer blocks forever.
D14.fix: use a predicate guarded by the mutex (while(!ready) cond_wait) so a prior signal is not lost.

states.d015a: RECEIVE on its channel; a timer pulse arrives every 400ms

D15.culprit: none: a periodic timer pulse drives one tick every 400ms; healthy.

D16.category: two servers call each other while handling (reentrancy)
axes: REPLY vs SEND in a 2-server cycle

states.d016c: SEND-blocked on d016b (which is not receiving)

D16.culprit: reentr_s1.c/reentr_s2.c: s1 MsgSends to s2 while handling the client; s2, handling s1's call, MsgSends back to s1, which is REPLY-blocked on s2 and not receiving.
D16.fix: do not call back synchronously while handling; reply first, or use a pulse / separate worker for the cross-call.

states.d017a: READY at boosted prio 15, holds mx, preempted

D17.culprit: prio_ceiling.c: the mutex is PTHREAD_PRIO_PROTECT with ceiling 15; the low holder is only boosted to 15, below the prio-20 hog, so it is preempted and the prio-30 waiter is starved.
D17.fix: raise the ceiling to >= the highest user priority (30), or use PTHREAD_PRIO_INHERIT.

D18.category: behaviour depends on a config file not in the capture
axes: cause is not in the provided source

states.d018a: RECEIVE on its channel; the upstream it should pull from is named in an absent config file

D18.culprit: need_conf.c: it reads /var/qd/D18/upstream.conf (not shipped with the capture) to learn its upstream; without it the process just waits. You cannot tell from the source whether this is a bug or a deployment/data problem.
D18.fix: cannot be determined from the capture; needs upstream.conf / the deployment config.

D19.category: server waits for a second message before replying
axes: timeout armed on the wrong state

states.d019a: REPLY-blocked on d019b (TimerTimeout armed on RECEIVE, so it does not fire)
states.d019b: RECEIVE, waiting for a 'body' message that never comes

D19.culprit: twomsg_srv.c: the server MsgReceives twice (header then body) before replying, but the client sends only one message per request, so it blocks on the second receive and the client stays REPLY-blocked. The client's TimerTimeout uses _NTO_TIMEOUT_RECEIVE, which does not guard its MsgSend.
D19.fix: reply after the single request (or have the client send both header and body); arm the client guard with _NTO_TIMEOUT_REPLY|_NTO_TIMEOUT_SEND.

states.d020d: RUNNING, spinning on a flag never set

D20.culprit: lowfix_srv.c: prio-12 fixed-priority server starved by the prio-20 hog (d020c) while the prio-30 client (d020a) is REPLY-blocked. Independently, spin_flag.c (d020d) busy-waits on a flag nothing sets.
D20.fix: server: drop fixed priority / raise above the hog. spinner: set the flag from the real path or block instead of spin.

axes: an idle worker read as stuck

states.d021a: running; dispatches to both workers every 300ms

D21.culprit: none: the dispatcher sends a job to each worker every 300ms and both reply; healthy. A snapshot catches a worker parked in RECEIVE.

D22.category: single-thread send to its own channel

states.d022a: SEND-blocked on its own channel (no thread is receiving)

D22.culprit: selfsend.c: the only thread ConnectAttaches to its own channel and MsgSends, but there is no second thread to MsgReceive, so it blocks on SEND forever.
D22.fix: receive on the channel from a separate thread, or do not message your own channel synchronously.

D23.category: low fixed-priority server starved; send guard set too long
axes: timeout present but value far too large

states.d023a: REPLY-blocked on d023b (TimerTimeout armed, but for 3600s)

D23.culprit: lowfix_srv.c: prio-12 fixed-priority server starved by the prio-20 hog. pp_client.c arms a REPLY timeout but the value is 1*1000*1000*1000*3600 ns (3600s), so the '1s guard' never fires within the window.
D23.fix: server: drop fixed priority / raise above the hog. client: set the guard to 1e9 ns (1s), not 3600e9.

D24.category: absurd sleep from an arithmetic bug
D24.culprit: longsleep.c: intended ~1s backoff, but ts.tv_sec = base*1000 with base=3600 yields 3,600,000 seconds; it ticks once then sleeps effectively forever.
D24.fix: set the backoff to the intended value (e.g. tv_sec=1), not base*1000.
